neighbours.label: ' to' / ' for' right after an effort noun (campaign, efforts, strategy, initiative) when a fight-the-problem verb such as combat, tackle or eradicate is expected next
fire: Health ministers from twelve countries met in Geneva to coordinate international efforts to combat the spread of tuberculosis.
The governor signed a bill that funds a statewide campaign to stamp out human trafficking.
Police chiefs presented a five-year strategy for tackling knife crime in the capital.
The foundation has donated millions to the worldwide drive to eradicate malaria by 2040.
Lawmakers praised the bank as a dependable partner in confronting money laundering.
The United Nations renewed its global programme to combat illegal wildlife poaching.
Aid groups say the new drug gives clinics a powerful weapon for fighting cholera outbreaks.
The mayor promised to double funding for the city's efforts to curb opioid addiction.
quiet: Health ministers from twelve countries flew to Geneva and listened to a long report about tuberculosis.
The governor gave the signed bill to a clerk, who carried it to the archive.
Police chiefs presented medals to five officers for long service in the capital.
The foundation has donated millions to a museum that documents the history of malaria.
Lawmakers said the bank had moved its headquarters to a quieter part of the city.
The United Nations sent its annual wildlife report to every member government.
Aid groups say the new drug is delivered to clinics in boxes packed for the heat.
The mayor went to the hospital to thank nurses who treat opioid patients.

notes: Card: peak ' to' x17 of 32, top examples 'Efforts to Combat Identity Theft', 'tool for saving', 'partner in confronting'; the + direction suppresses fight/combat, so this pole promotes them. Probes: 'campaign to eradicate polio' 0.47, 'initiative to curb gang violence' 0.24, 'strategy for tackling' 0.22; ordinary 'to' (walked to the market, wanted to learn) 0.00. English probes are well below the corpus max, so the median may land near the 0.20 line.
